data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Mexico factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Mexico performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how performance relates to student background and school experiences. PISA 2022 used two two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different combinations of test questions, plus a student background questionnaire and a school principal questionnaire. The factsheet reports descriptive indicators such as mean performance trends (2018–2022), proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6 shares), and subgroup differences (e.g., socioeconomic status quintiles and gender gaps). For Mexico, 34% of students reached at least Level 2 in mathematics (OECD average: 69%), 53% in reading (OECD average: 74%), and 49% in science (OECD average: 76%). It also reports that Mexico’s performance declined in mathematics and science compared with 2018, and that socioeconomic status is a predictor of mathematics performance, accounting for 10% of variation in Mexico. The document does not provide ML model performance metrics or an explicit PV/missing-data handling procedure in the excerpt, so the results should be interpreted as survey-based descriptive reporting rather than causal or predictive modeling.
